note: BOOK-INTERNAL INCONSISTENCY rather than an arithmetic slip — the key contradicts ITSELF, which is the strongest evidence class available here. The key for 3.4 can only exclude (f) by reading "a component of a vector" as the SCALAR coefficient A_x, so that (f) collapses into case (b) (scalar + vector). But the key for 3.5(b) answers the statement "each component of a vector is always a scalar" with F — explicitly denying that a component is a scalar. Under the key's own 3.5(b) ruling a component is a VECTOR of the same dimensions as its parent, and then the key's own rule for (e) (vectors of equal dimensions may be added) makes (f) permissible. The CHAPTER TEXT supports the vector reading too: section 3.5 resolves A = (lambda)a + (mu)b and calls (lambda)a and (mu)b the component VECTORS, and Eq. (3.16b) writes A = A_x i + A_y j + A_z k. Two of the six sub-parts therefore cannot both be right under one consistent definition of "component". Our answer follows the definition the chapter and the 3.5(b) key both use. FOR MAINTAINER ADJUDICATION — the alternative is to keep the key's reading and record it as a preserved book defect.
